newsitem.title: FRANCE: European Forum establish by air cargo industry.
newsitem.headline: European Forum establish by air cargo industry.

text.p: Key players in the European air cargo industry Friday launched the Forum for Air Cargo in Europe (FACE) as the first European umbrella body to promote the industry and improve both quality and performance standards for the final customers.

"We felt that it was absolutely vital that all the players got together including the most important of all, the shipper," Robert Arendal senior vice president and chief executive officer of Cargolux told a news conference.
FACE represents airlines, freight forwarders and shippers - exporters and importers - both individually and through trade organisations.

FACE's setting up follows recommendations by the European air shippers council (EASC) in its air freight 2000 document issued in September 1995 and a meeting of interested parties in mid-February this year.
EASC secretary Chris Welsh said "everyone is concerned that FACE should be issue based and not just another talking shop." EASC will provide the secretariat for FACE.
Following Friday's meeting Welsh said "we have decided to set up a working group to look at performance standards so that we can promote best practices in the industry."
"We are looking at challenging but achievable standards to achieve quality and reliability," he stated.
Roger Allen director airlines at MSAS said "eventually one would only deal with those who meet these standards".

Welsh said the working group will be assisted by the initial studies already carried out by the UK Air Freight Forum, which will now be adapted to a European context. The UK Forum held its first meeting last November as a tripartite body to tackle problems in the UK air cargo industry
The working group "will, within four to six weeks work to quickly identify the relevant performance standards. We set an end-year target but hopefully it could be before that," Welsh said.

MSAS's Allen said there could be six key standards of which one might be flown-as-booked and another vehicle offload times. Industry sources said no shows is anotheer problem area that can be measured.

"FACE is keeping its aims simple. But if necessary other partners might be consulted on specific issues such as customs or ground handling. Standards need to be set to simplify and clarify," Cargolux's Aren said.
"I can also see FACE coordinating Europe's relationship to other similar groupings elsewhere in the world such as the Far East and the U.S.," he added.
Asked about the cargo fuel surcharge MSAS's Allen said "there was a consensus that if the Forum had already existed, last year's fuel surcharge would have been introduced in a modified fashion".

David Woodward general manager cargo at Virgin Atlantic said in answer to a question that "potential savings from improved service standards copuld on a owrldwide basis amount to billions of dollars" although he stressed it was difficult to give an accurate estimate. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
